title: Validate checklist step: detect first streaming session (Hosted API)
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Goal
Define and implement the server-side validation signal for the guided onboarding checklist step: “Use streaming responses” (aka “first streaming session”). This ticket covers the definition, edge cases, and computation approach so the Console can reliably mark the step complete with minimal user confusion.

Context
The guided onboarding checklist (Phase 1: Hosted API) includes an early step encouraging users to try streaming (SSE) for chat/text generation. We want to auto-complete the step when we can verify a project has successfully initiated a streaming response.

Non-goals
- We are not building a new streaming transport (still SSE over HTTPS).
- We are not attempting to validate “best practices” for streaming (client backpressure, reconnection) beyond “a streaming response was started”.
- We are not instrumenting prompt/token content (explicitly prohibited).

Proposed definition (v1)
A “streaming session” is considered successful for checklist completion when:
1) A request is made to a supported completion endpoint with streaming enabled (e.g., stream=true), AND
2) The server begins sending a streaming response (at least one streaming chunk/delta is emitted), AND
3) The request is authorized and routed to a model successfully (i.e., not a 401/403/404/5xx before streaming starts).

Notes on completion semantics:
- We do NOT require the stream to finish cleanly ([DONE] / normal close). Many legitimate first attempts disconnect due to user code/terminal exit; requiring a graceful completion creates false negatives.
- We DO require “at least one chunk sent” to avoid counting requests that never actually streamed (e.g., client disconnect before first bytes, upstream failure before first token).

Scope / where this is computed
Compute on backend using gateway/request logs + streaming lifecycle markers. Console should not have to “guess” based on client events alone.

Implementation plan
1) Add/consume a streaming lifecycle signal from the gateway
- Preferred signal: gateway emits a metrics/log line when first response bytes are flushed for a streaming request (e.g., stream_first_chunk_at).
- If we already have a “response_first_byte_at” measurement, ensure it’s emitted for streaming routes and distinguishable from non-streaming.
- Must include: org_id, project_id, request_id, route, model, region, timestamp, and an allowlisted boolean for streaming_enabled.
- Must NOT include: prompt text, tool arguments, raw tokens, or user message content.

2) Validator logic (per project)
- Add validator job/query in checklist validation service:
  - Input: project_id
  - Condition: exists at least one request in last N days (N=30 for lookback, configurable) where streaming_enabled=true AND stream_first_chunk_at is present.
  - Output: set checklist step “first_streaming_session” completed_at = min(stream_first_chunk_at).
- Idempotency:
  - If step already completed, do nothing (do not overwrite earlier timestamp).
  - Dedupe by request_id when ingesting lifecycle signals.

3) Validation latency expectations
- Target: checklist reflects completion within 1–3 minutes of the first streaming chunk.
- Acceptable: up to 10 minutes during telemetry pipeline delays (beta). Console copy should mention “may take a minute to update”.

4) Supported endpoints (Phase 1)
- /v1/chat/completions (stream=true)
- /v1/completions (stream=true) if still supported publicly
Explicitly out of scope: embeddings and rerank (non-streaming).

Edge cases / decisions
1) Client disconnects mid-stream (common in first attempts)
- If at least one chunk was emitted, count as completed.
- If disconnect occurs before first chunk, do not count.

2) Retries
- Streaming requests are often not safe to retry automatically once bytes are emitted.
- However, users may implement their own retry loop.
- We should count the first request_id that reaches first chunk; multiple attempts are fine.

3) 499 / client closed request
- If 499 but stream_first_chunk_at exists, count.
- If 499 and no chunk, do not count.

4) Partial auth issues / wrong key env
- 401/403 should never count.
- This step should be independent of “prod key” step; it should complete for test keys too (we want early success). Prod/test gating remains a separate checklist step.

5) Tool-calling + streaming
- If stream=true and first chunk emitted, count regardless of whether tool calling is enabled.

6) SDK differences
- Python/TS/Go implement SSE slightly differently; validator must not depend on client behavior. Only gateway lifecycle.

7) Multi-region / eventual consistency
- Validator should search across regions (or rely on centralized logs). If regional pipeline is degraded, step completion may lag; we should alert via telemetry health (ENG-23125).

Telemetry / eventing
- When the step is marked complete server-side, emit onboarding telemetry event:
  - event_name: onboarding_checklist_step_completed
  - properties (allowlisted): step_key=first_streaming_session, project_id, org_id, completed_at, source=validator, request_route (optional), model_family (optional)
- Ensure property allowlist is aligned with privacy review; no request payload fields.

Acceptance criteria
- A streaming request that emits at least one chunk results in the “first_streaming_session” step becoming completed for that project.
- Completion updates show up in Console within target latency (<=3 min typical; <=10 min worst-case during beta).
- 401/403/429/5xx without any streamed chunks does not complete the step.
- Client disconnect after at least one chunk still completes the step.
- No prompt/tool payload content is logged or emitted as event properties.
- Add tests covering: success, disconnect-before-first-chunk, disconnect-after-first-chunk, non-streaming request, unauthorized, rate-limited.

Testing plan
- Unit tests for validator query/filtering logic.
- Integration test with synthetic gateway log entries:
  - Create two records: stream=true with stream_first_chunk_at set; expect completion.
  - Create record: stream=true but no stream_first_chunk_at; expect not completed.
  - Create record: status=401 with stream=true; expect not completed.
- E2E (in ENG-23124): run a streaming quickstart call in CI environment and assert checklist step transitions.

Rollout / risk
- Roll behind onboarding checklist feature flag. Validation signal can ship before UI GA, but do not emit user-visible completion outside cohort.
- Watch for false positives if stream_first_chunk_at is incorrectly set for non-streaming responses. Add a guard requiring streaming_enabled=true.

Links
- Initiative: PM-482
- Related engineering: ENG-23112 (emit events), ENG-23111 (state model), ENG-23124 (E2E)
- PR (implementation): sources/github/redwood/pr-48293.json

Activity / comments

2026-02-11 (Amara Diallo): Noted 499 patterns in logs; proposed logic above (count if first chunk exists).
2026-02-18 (Hannah Rivera): Implemented validator + tests; added guard streaming_enabled=true AND stream_first_chunk_at != null.
2026-02-26 (Leila Farouk): QA found lag in eu-west pipeline; step completion delayed ~12m. Logged follow-up to telemetry health alerts.
